title: When Israel Through the Desert Passed
description: When Israel Through the Desert Passed in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Benjamin Beddome wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 118.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: When Is-rael through the des-ert passed, A fie-ry pil-lar went be-fore To guide them through the drea-ry waste And les-sen the fa-tigues they bore.

lines: When Israel through the desert passed,
A fiery pillar went before
To guide them through the dreary waste
And lessen the fatigues they bore.
Such is Thy glorious Word, O God!
’Tis for our light and guidance giv’n;
It sheds its luster all abroad
And points the path to bliss and heav’n.
It fills the soul with sweet delight
And quickens its inactive powers;
It sets our wand’ring footsteps right,
Displays Thy love, and kindles ours.
Its promises rejoice our hearts,
Its doctrines are divinely true;
While highest wisdom it imparts,
It comforts and instructs us too.
Ye favored lands, that have this Word,
Ye saints, who feel its saving power,
Unite your tongues to praise the Lord
And His distinguished grace adore!

licence: Public domain: Benjamin Beddome died in 1795.
credits: Words by Benjamin Beddome (1717–1795), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
